title: Omega-3 and DHA in Pregnancy: Food Sources and Supplement Cautions
excerpt: Why DHA matters for fetal development, low-mercury fish options, and when to ask a clinician about supplements
content:
## Introduction
During pregnancy, providing adequate nutrition for both mother and fetus is crucial. One of the most important nutrients is Omega-3 and DHA. In this article, we will explore the role of DHA in fetal development, food sources rich in Omega-3 and DHA, and precautions when taking supplements.

## The Role of DHA
DHA (Docosahexaenoic acid) is an essential Omega-3 fatty acid that plays a critical role in fetal brain and eye development. According to the World Health Organization (WHO), DHA supports fetal brain and nervous system development, as well as reduces the risk of heart disease and arthritis.

## Food Sources Rich in Omega-3 and DHA
There are many food sources rich in Omega-3 and DHA, including:
* Salmon: This is one of the richest sources of Omega-3 and DHA.
* Sardines: Sardines are another rich source of Omega-3 and DHA.
* Anchovies: Anchovies are a rich source of Omega-3 and DHA, as well as other nutrients like vitamin D and selenium.
* Eggs: Eggs are a good source of Omega-3 and DHA.
* Nuts and seeds: Nuts and seeds like walnuts, chia seeds, and flaxseeds are rich in Omega-3 and DHA.

## Precautions When Taking Supplements
While food is the best source of Omega-3 and DHA, supplements may be necessary in some cases. However, before taking supplements, you should consult with your clinician to ensure safety and efficacy.

## Foods to Avoid
During pregnancy, you should avoid eating the following foods:
* High-mercury fish: Fish high in mercury like shark, swordfish, and king mackerel can harm the fetus.
* Undercooked food: Undercooked food like sushi, sashimi, and raw eggs can contain harmful bacteria.

## Conclusion
Omega-3 and DHA are essential nutrients for fetal development. You can provide adequate Omega-3 and DHA to your fetus through food sources rich in these nutrients. However, before taking supplements, you should consult with your clinician to ensure safety and efficacy. For more information on prenatal nutrition, you can visit our [website](/blog/prenatal-nutrition).

## When to Consult a Clinician
If you have any questions or concerns about prenatal nutrition, you should consult with your clinician. Your clinician can provide you with specific information and advice on how to provide adequate nutrition for your fetus.
